children.text:
I'm curios what drives you to archiving invoices yourself. I had a German startup and am friends with various people owning German companies up to about 150 employees, and all of them ended up with whatever service their tax advisor uses (typically Datev, but there are some alternatives). It costs a couple bucks to pay them to store the invoices for 10 years, but compared to the price of anything else from the tax adivisor it's basically free

I would immediately get your requirement if it was about other legal requirements. But hearing it for tax purposes is a bit unusual. Are you doing your own taxes (hat off to you if you do)

Do you have a certificate for GoBD compliance? Just because it claims to support archival requirements doesn’t make it compliant. If not, you can only wait an see, go to court. Sadly we have Beweislastumkehr in taxation law.

You have documentation/storage duties due to a few other laws, too. But you don't need Exchange to have revision secure/tamper proof e-mail archives, even if you are on MS365. There are plenty of services and solutions available for that. We, for example, use the premium version of Mailpiler [1].

[1] https://www.mailpiler.org/

children.author: sevindob
children.text: You dont pick and choose, If you're a regulated business, all your email must be stored that way.

source.text:
Not all mail is tax relevant. 
While I’m not a lawyer I’m pretty sure (especially for a freelancer and small(er) company there is nothing wrong with forwarding your invoices@example.com directly to a service like DATEV (german provider for “tax software”, simply speaking) as almost anyone with a digital invoice workflow has. There you should have all the needs fulfilled.
